tagline.text: Wild whale sharks with no feeding, and deep coral walls

location.label: Location
location.text: Padre Burgos, Limasawa, and Panaon Island area, Southern Leyte

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱3,000–6,000 per person (per day, including diving)

children.text: A deep bay cutting into the southern tip of Leyte Island, a quiet hidden gem for divers. Coral walls close to shore and resident sea turtles and macro life can be seen year-round, and from
November to May
, you can snorkel with wild whale sharks that are never fed.
Sogod Bay is a bay reaching more than
30km

inland between the Southern Leyte mainland and Panaon Island to the southeast. Its waters are deep and the seas relatively calm, so just a few dozen meters offshore, coral shelves drop off into steep walls. Diving is centered on four areas: Padre Burgos on the west coast, Limasawa Island at the bay's southern entrance, and Panaon Island and Liloan to the east, with more than 20 dive sites across them.
What makes this place special is the whale sharks. From
November to May

, as plankton increases, whale sharks enter the bay — but unlike Oslob in Cebu, no one feeds or holds them in place; instead, divers seek out sharks passing naturally and swim alongside them briefly. Sighting odds vary day to day, but travelers seeking an encounter with wild whale sharks come here specifically for that reason. The waters around Panaon Island were designated the Panaon Island Protected Seascape by law in

The signature site, Napantao, is a marine protected area off the west coast of Panaon Island, where soft coral and sea fan-covered walls host schools of anthias and whitetip reef sharks. Medicare Point off Padre Burgos has weak current, making it easy even for beginners to spot sea turtles, while the area under the pier and the black-sand bottom nearby turn up macro life such as frogfish, seahorses, ghost pipefish, and flamboyant cuttlefish. Visibility reaches
on good days, and water temperature stays around
year-round.
Limasawa Island, at the bay's mouth, also holds historical significance as the site of the first Easter Mass in the Philippines, celebrated by Magellan's expedition on
March 31, 1521

. With no large resorts or busy strips, it's a quiet fishing area that particularly suits divers who want to dive at an easy pace away from the crowds, and beginners working toward an Open Water certification.

When a spotter on an outrigger boat locates a whale shark, you enter the water on a signal and swim alongside it as it passes. Feeding and touching are prohibited, and you sometimes need to swim quickly through the swell, so being a confident swimmer makes the experience more enjoyable.

Panaon Island's signature wall dive, with soft coral, giant sea fans, and schools of purple anthias making for a spectacular scene. Current can run here, so it suits divers with some prior experience.
About
1 hour
by boat from Padre Burgos, the waters around Limasawa Island are known for deep walls draped in black coral and large sponges. With luck, you may also encounter big schools of fish and sharks.

blocks.title: Meeting Sea Turtles at Medicare Point

children.text: Right off the coast of Padre Burgos, this site has weak current and a broad coral shelf, making it good for trial dives or beginner training. Green and hawksbill sea turtles appear frequently.
The area beneath the Padre Burgos pier and the black-sand bottom near Malitbog are popular with divers hunting small creatures. Guides help you find frogfish, ribbon eels, and pygmy seahorses.
On a hill on Limasawa Island stands a shrine and monument commemorating the first Easter Mass in the Philippines. Climb the steps for a sweeping view of Sogod Bay and the Bohol Sea.

blocks.title: Working Toward an Open Water Certification

children.text: The calm bay and nearby coastal sites make for a good training environment. Dive resorts in Padre Burgos offer 3–4 day certification courses.

blocks.title: A View of the Bay from the Hills

children.text: From the hills and mountain-road viewpoints behind Sogod town, you can see the whole of Sogod Bay stretching out between the mountains on either side. The sunset over the bay is beautiful when you climb up in the late afternoon.

There are also ferries from Ubay in Bohol to Bato in Southern Leyte, and from Surigao in Mindanao toward Panaon Island, making it easy to link this trip with Bohol or Siargao. Schedules change often, so check the shipping line's notices.

Multicabs and tricycles run along the coastal road in Padre Burgos. Most dive resorts launch boats directly from in front of the resort for boat dives and whale shark tours, so you won't often need to arrange separate transport.
Limasawa Island is about
30 minutes to 1 hour
by scheduled or chartered outrigger boat from the Padre Burgos pier.
Diving is possible year-round, but the best timing depends on your goal. To see whale sharks, aim for
November–May
, with sightings said to be more frequent during
March–April

. Since these are wild animals, though, sightings vary significantly by year and by day, so it's best to keep your expectations modest. This period is also the resort high season, so rooms fill up quickly around holidays.
From
November to February
, the northeast monsoon brings frequent rain, and the seas around Limasawa and Napantao, outside the bay, can turn rough on some days. From
May to October
, the sea is calm on many days, making it easier to reach the farther sites, but a typhoon in the area can halt sailings for days at a time. Water temperature stays around
year-round, so a 3mm wetsuit is enough.

Most lodging is at dive resorts lining the coastal road in Padre Burgos. Long-running options like Peter's Dive Resort and Sogod Bay Scuba Resort are among the best known, ranging from about
a night for a diver's dormitory bed up to
for a private room with a sea view. Booking a diving package often bundles a discount on lodging and diving together. For more urban conveniences, staying in Maasin, the provincial capital about
30 minutes
to the northwest, is another option.
Padre Burgos town has small restaurants, a bakery, and roast-chicken stalls, but most close around
7 PM

, so dinner is often eaten at the resort restaurant. Being a fishing area, freshly grilled fish, squid, and crab dishes, along with kinilaw, are both fresh and inexpensive. Leyte's traditional snacks binagol and moron are easy to find at Maasin's market.
ATMs are very scarce in Padre Burgos, and there are no large supermarkets. Bring enough cash for diving costs and daily expenses from Tacloban or Maasin.
Whale shark tours depart early in the morning depending on sighting reports. Sign up with your resort the evening before and wait for word.
You'll need to fin and swim quickly to keep up with a whale shark. If you're not confident in your stamina, ask for a life vest or a buoy.
Jellyfish season occurs at times, so wear a rash guard or a thin wetsuit, and use reef-safe sunscreen.
Wall dives at Napantao and Limasawa can have current, so it's safer to be honest with your guide about your recent diving experience and log.
Power outages happen occasionally, so charge your camera battery and any spare batteries in advance.
You need to wait at least
18–24 hours
after diving before flying, so plan your last day around Limasawa Island sightseeing or snorkeling instead of diving.
If you're combining this trip with Bohol or Siargao, checking ferry schedules toward Bato or Surigao in advance will make your onward travel smoother.
Under the ordinance, whale shark tours allow snorkeling only (scuba is prohibited), with a maximum observation time of
3 hours
. It takes about
1 hour 30 minutes
by boat out to the meeting point and the whole day runs
6–8 hours
, so plan a light dive schedule for that day.

Whale sharks are wild animals. Touching, blocking their path, chasing, and flash photography are all prohibited, and set distance and group-size rules must be followed. Related regulations and fees can change under local government policy, so check the latest notices.
There is no major hospital or decompression chamber around Padre Burgos. Avoid pushing your dive limits and carry dive insurance.
During boat dives, currents and swell can pick up suddenly, so carry a surface marker buoy (SMB) and stay close to your guide.
During typhoon season (
July–December
), ferry and boat sailings can be cancelled, so build slack into your schedule.
Don't step on or grab coral, and don't take shells or coral fragments. Violating protected-area rules can result in a fine.
Avoid drinking alcohol and prolonged exposure to strong sun after diving, and drink plenty of water.
